decisions.rationale: Lead Tyranitar+Excadrill sand core: Sand Stream gives Excadrill 280 Spe outspeeding everything, High Horsepower is 2x SE on Metagross/Klefki/Incineroar, Tyranitar resists Dragapult's Shadow Ball (0.5x) and Fire Blast (0.5x) while Excadrill is immune to Thunderbolt. Focus Sash protects Excadrill from Fake Out. Back: Mega Gengar for Shadow Tag trapping and Energy Ball to answer Rotom-Wash (Levitate blocks Excadrill); Houndoom for Flamethrower on Metagross/Klefki and Dark Pulse on Dragapult, with Flash Fire to absorb Incineroar Fire moves aimed at Tyranitar.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead plan: Tyranitar+Excadrill sand core. Key type facts confirmed: Tyranitar resists Dragapult Shadow Ball (0.5x) and Fire Blast (0.5x); Excadrill immune to Thunderbolt (Ground), neutral to Shadow Ball, weak to Fire Blast (2x). High Horsepower SE on Metagross (2x), Klefki (2x), Incineroar (2x), neutral on Dragapult. Iron Head SE on Serperior (2x). Rotom-Wash is the main Excadrill problem (Levitate blocks Ground, Iron Head 0.25x) — Gengar Energy Ball (2x SE) is the answer. Houndoom Dark Pulse SE on Dragapult (2x), Flamethrower SE on Metagross/Klefki/Serperior. Watch for Incineroar Fake Out+Intimidate lead disrupting Excadrill; Protect to dodge Fake Out. Opponent Mega is Metagross (Metagrossite). Klefki Prankster screens could slow us down — Gengar Taunt or Houndoom Flamethrower to break through.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult outspeeds the entire opponent team (213 vs max 200 Mega Gengar) and threatens OHKO on Gengar with Life Orb Shadow Ball. Rotom-Wash walls Excadrill completely (Levitate immune to High Horsepower, resists Iron Head 4x, neutral Rock Slide) and threatens both Tyranitar and Excadrill with 2x Hydro Pump. Incineroar in back provides Intimidate cycling, Fake Out disruption, and Parting Shot pivoting to handle Tauros-Aqua and physical threats. Mega Metagross brings Bullet Punch priority and Tough Claws Psychic Fangs to guarantee OHKO on Gengar while offering Steel-type bulk.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Dragapult + Rotom-Wash. Back: Incineroar + Metagross. Opponent's sand mode (Tyranitar + Excadrill) is the primary threat to neutralize early; Rotom-Wash is the hard counter. Mega Gengar Shadow Tag trapping is dangerous but Dragapult speed control keeps it in check. Serperior and Klefki benched for this game.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill Protects to preserve Focus Sash and full HP against potential double-targeting (Fire Blast 82-123% breaks Sash, then Hydro Pump KOs). Tyranitar Crunch hits Dragapult for 58.5-108% — possible OHKO, always heavy damage. If Dragapult Protects, only Crunch is wasted; Excadrill stays pristine for sand sweeping. Tyranitar survives Hydro Pump (47-70%) and remains functional. This hedges against the most common Turn 1 Protect from fast frail Dragapult while still applying maximum pressure.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead plan: Tyranitar+Excadrill sand core. Key damage calcs confirmed: TTar Crunch on Dragapult 58.5-108% (possible OHKO), Excadrill HHP on Dragapult 44.6-84.7% (combined with Crunch = guaranteed KO). Dragapult Fire Blast on Excadrill 81.8-122.5% (breaks Sash). Rotom Hydro Pump on Tyranitar 46.4-69.6%. Dragapult Shadow Ball on Tyranitar only 9.2-14.5% (TTar walls it). Excadrill Rock Slide on Rotom only 17.8-32.8% (spread). Rotom-Wash is the main Excadrill problem (Levitate blocks Ground, Iron Head 0.25x) — Gengar Energy Ball (2x SE) is the answer. Houndoom Dark Pulse SE on Dragapult (2x), Flamethrower SE on Metagross/Klefki/Serperior. Watch for Incineroar Fake Out+Intimidate lead disrupting Excadrill; Protect to dodge Fake Out. Opponent Mega is Metagross (Metagrossite). Klefki Prankster screens could slow us down — Gengar Taunt or Houndoom Flamethrower to break through.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult must Protect to avoid the 90.9–127.3% Crunch OHKO from Tyranitar. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump threatens Tyranitar for 46.4–82.3% while Rotom easily survives any combination of foe attacks (max ~76% from Crunch + Rock Slide). Switching Incineroar risks a High Horsepower OHKO (83.2–116.8%); staying in with Dragapult unprotected risks losing it immediately. This line preserves both mons and pressures the sand core.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Dragapult + Rotom-Wash. Back: Incineroar + Metagross. Opponent's sand mode (Tyranitar + Excadrill) is the primary threat to neutralize early; Rotom-Wash is the hard counter. Turn 1: Protect Dragapult from Tyranitar Crunch OHKO range, Hydro Pump Tyranitar to pressure sand setter. Mega Gengar Shadow Tag trapping is dangerous but Dragapult speed control keeps it in check.

decisions.rationale: Guaranteed KO on Dragapult: Excadrill HHP (44.6-84.7%, goes first at 280 Spe) + Tyranitar Crunch (58.5-108%, 2x SE) = 103.1-192.7% combined, killing Dragapult at 93% HP. Dragapult's Protect is at reduced success rate so they likely attack — Fire Blast on Excadrill is absorbed by Focus Sash (Excadrill survives at 1 HP, immune to Sandstorm as Steel-type). Rotom likely Hydro Pumps Tyranitar (46.4-69.6%, leaving TTar at ~30-53%) — acceptable cost to remove the opponent's fastest Life Orb threat. Even if opponent double-targets Excadrill, Dragapult still dies to Crunch and Tyranitar stays full. Removing Dragapult shifts the game firmly in our favor with sand rush Excadrill still threatening at 280 Spe.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead plan: Tyranitar+Excadrill sand core. Turn 2 plan: Crunch+HHP on Dragapult for guaranteed KO. Excadrill Steel-type immune to Sandstorm so survives at 1 HP after Sash breaks. After Dragapult KO, opponent brings in one of Incineroar/Metagross/Klefki/Serperior. Next turn: Excadrill at 1 HP can still attack at 280 Spe but any hit KOs it — consider switching to Gengar-Mega (Shadow Tag traps, Energy Ball hits Rotom SE) or Houndoom depending on what comes in. Tyranitar at ~30-53% HP is vulnerable — may need to switch out if facing Metagross (Meteor Mash SE on TTar) or Serperior (Leaf Storm SE). Priority threats: Metagross Bullet Punch picks off 1 HP Excadrill.

decisions.rationale: Switch in Gengar (Mega Evolves → Shadow Tag). Gengar-Mega Energy Ball does 49.7-92.8% to Rotom-Wash (pre-Mega calc; 170 SpA post-Mega will be even higher), and with Tyranitar Helping Hand it becomes a guaranteed KO. Shadow Tag traps Rotom-Wash, preventing Volt Switch escape. Gengar's Ghost typing grants Fake Out immunity if Incineroar comes in, and Taunt shuts down Klefki screens. Houndoom's best option (Dark Pulse 38.2-72%) cannot KO Rotom-Wash from 88%, and Flamethrower is NVE (21.7-40.8%). Tyranitar stays active at 100% HP.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead plan: Tyranitar+Excadrill sand core. Gengar Taunt shuts Klefki screens. Houndoom better vs Metagross (Flamethrower SE 2x) and Serperior (Flamethrower SE 2x, Leaf Storm NVE 0.5x on Fire/Dark, Flash Fire immune to Fire). Opponent Mega is Metagross (Metagrossite, Tough Claws, 130-162 Spe). Gengar-Mega outspeeds Metagross-Mega (165-200 vs 130-162). Watch for Incineroar Darkest Lariat SE on Gengar (2x). Next turn plan: Gengar-Mega Energy Ball + Tyranitar Helping Hand on Rotom-Wash for guaranteed KO, unless opponent's incoming Pokémon threatens Gengar-Mega (Metagross Meteor Mash, Incineroar Darkest Lariat) — then consider Protect/redirect. Tyranitar at 100% HP, sand active 7 turns.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Excadrill to guarantee KO through Focus Sash: Fire Blast (64.5–123.8%) + Hydro Pump (85.7–160%) = minimum 150.2%. Excadrill moves first and can damage Dragapult, and Tyranitar Crunch likely KOs Dragapult afterward, but eliminating Sand Rush Excadrill is worth the trade. Rotom-Wash then dominates Tyranitar 1v1 with Hydro Pump, and Incineroar + Metagross wait in back. Switching Dragapult risks Excadrill predicting with High Horsepower (83–117% on Incineroar, possible OHKO); staying in and trading is more consistent.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lead: Dragapult + Rotom-Wash. Back: Incineroar + Metagross. Opponent's sand mode (Tyranitar + Excadrill) is the primary threat; Rotom-Wash is the hard counter. Turn 1: Protected Dragapult, Hydro Pump missed Tyranitar. Turn 2: double-targeted Excadrill to break sash and remove Sand Rush speed control, accepting Dragapult likely falls to Crunch. Opponent's unrevealed two: from {Gengar-Mega, Tauros-Aqua, Gholdengo, Houndoom}. Mega Gengar Shadow Tag remains a trapping threat to respect.

decisions.rationale: Metagross is the optimal switch: it resists Rock Slide (10-15%), threatens Tyranitar with Tough Claws-boosted Meteor Mash (likely OHKO range after Mega), and Psychic Fangs OHKOs any Gengar switch-in. Mega Metagross outspeeds Tyranitar and doesn't take Sandstorm chip. Incineroar's Intimidate+FakeOut is weaker here — Rock Slide still does 45-63% and Fake Out chip is negligible. Metagross establishes immediate offensive pressure and pairs well with Rotom-Wash's Hydro Pump to secure the KO on Tyranitar if it stays in.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Dragapult and Excadrill traded. Sent Metagross to pair with Rotom-Wash against Tyranitar + unrevealed back. Opponent's two unrevealed from {Gengar-Mega, Tauros-Aqua, Gholdengo, Houndoom}. Mega Metagross Tough Claws Meteor Mash threatens Tyranitar; Psychic Fangs OHKOs Gengar. Incineroar still in back with Intimidate and Fake Out available.

decisions.rationale: Metagross Psychic Fangs is a guaranteed OHKO on Gengar (149-212%), so we must Protect. Mega Evolving activates Shadow Tag, trapping both foes and shutting off Rotom's Volt Switch. Tyranitar Crunch does 43-74% to Metagross (SE 2x) as chip damage with a 20% Def drop chance. Next turn: Helping Hand + Energy Ball on trapped Rotom for the KO, then focus fire Metagross.
decisions.notebook: Metagross Psychic Fangs = GUARANTEED OHKO on Gengar (148.9-211.7%), even post-Mega — must Protect when Metagross is active and not locked. Metagross Meteor Mash on Tyranitar = 47.3-67.6%. Tyranitar Crunch on Metagross = 42.8-73.5% (SE 2x). Gengar-Mega Shadow Ball on Metagross = 62-116.1% pre-Mega (post-Mega higher, possible OHKO). Gengar-Mega outspeeds Metagross-Mega (165-200 vs 130-162). Shadow Tag traps both foes, prevents Volt Switch. Turn 4 plan: Helping Hand + Energy Ball (Mega) on Rotom for KO (Shadow Tag prevents escape). Then focus Metagross with Shadow Ball + Crunch. Houndoom in back for Metagross (Flamethrower SE) and Serperior (Flamethrower SE, Flash Fire immune to Fire). Watch for Incineroar Darkest Lariat SE on Gengar (2x).

decisions.rationale: Double-target Gengar with priority Bullet Punch (Mega, Tough Claws: 32.6–67.5%) + Dark Pulse (49.1–96.3%). Combined range 81.7–163.8% gives ~75–85% chance to KO Mega Gengar before it can trap us permanently with Shadow Tag. Bullet Punch goes first (+1 priority), so even if the opponent uses Helping Hand + Shadow Ball, Gengar faints before firing if the combined damage KOs. If Gengar falls, Metagross survives Tyranitar's single hit; if not, we trade Metagross for a heavily damaged Gengar and still have Rotom-Wash + Incineroar against Tyranitar + unrevealed. Mega Evolving Metagross maximizes Bullet Punch damage via Tough Claws.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Dragapult and Excadrill traded early. Opponent's remaining unrevealed is one of {Tauros-Aqua, Gholdengo, Houndoom}. Gengar is the Mega threat with Shadow Tag — removing it is top priority. Incineroar still in back with Intimidate and Chople Berry, walls both Tyranitar and Gengar STABs. Sandstorm from Smooth Rock Tyranitar has ~6 turns left.

decisions.rationale: Gengar (200 Spe) outspeeds Metagross/Metagross-Mega (90-162), so Shadow Ball KOs Metagross at 31% HP (77% min dmg) before it can use Psychic Fangs (which would OHKO Gengar). Only Bullet Punch (+1 pri) could precede, but 40 BP neutral won't KO Gengar. Splitting Tyranitar's Crunch onto Rotom (28.7-53.6% neutral) guarantees value from at least one slot regardless of which foe Protects, and preserves Gengar + Shadow Tag for the 2v1. Double-targeting Metagross risks both moves wasted to a Protect; Helping Hand+Energy Ball on Rotom risks total whiff if Rotom Protects and Metagross then KOs Gengar.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega (200 Spe) always outspeeds Metagross-Mega (130-162); Shadow Ball guaranteed KO on Metagross at 31% (77-140.6%). Metagross Psychic Fangs = guaranteed OHKO on Gengar (119.7-170.8%) — must prevent Metagross from ever acting vs Gengar. Tyranitar Crunch on Rotom-Wash = 28.7-53.6% neutral (Sitrus Berry may trigger). HH+Energy Ball = guaranteed KO on Rotom at 82% (90.4-168%). Shadow Tag traps both foes, prevents Volt Switch. Houndoom in back: Flash Fire immune to Fire, Life Orb, Flamethrower SE on Metagross+Serperior, Sucker Punch for priority. Opponent 4th mon is one of Incineroar (Intimidate/Chople, Darkest Lariat SE on Gengar), Klefki (Prankster T-Wave/Screens, Taunt with Gengar to shut down), or Serperior (Contrary Leaf Storm SE on Tyranitar, 146-181 Spe slower than Gengar). If Metagross KO'd this turn, next turn focus Rotom with Energy Ball+Crunch. Save Houndoom for Serperior or as Tyranitar replacement if needed.

decisions.rationale: Metagross at 31% dies to any attack from either foe. Protect (+4 priority) blocks all incoming damage. Mega Evolving now gives Tough Claws for next turn. Rotom Volt Switch into Gengar-Mega deals chip (29–53%) and pivots to Incineroar despite Shadow Tag — Volt Switch's text explicitly bypasses trapping. Incineroar's Intimidate then drops Tyranitar's Attack, and next turn Fake Out can flinch Tyranitar while Mega Metagross threatens Gengar with Tough Claws-boosted Bullet Punch.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Dragapult and Excadrill fainted. Opponent's last unrevealed is one of {Tauros-Aqua, Gholdengo, Houndoom}. Gengar-Mega has Shadow Tag — only pivot moves escape. Metagross holds our only Mega Stone; Mega Evolving grants Tough Claws. Incineroar carries Chople Berry and Intimidate, walls both Tyranitar and Gengar STABs. Sandstorm from Smooth Rock Tyranitar persists.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Bullet Punch (pri +1) is a guaranteed KO on Gengar at 37% before Shadow Ball can resolve. Gengar must Protect to survive. Tyranitar Crunches Metagross (26.7-43.9% vs 31% HP — possible KO). If Crunch KOs, we're in great shape with Gengar alive. If not, Metagross is at ~0-4% and easily finished next turn. Shadow Tag traps both foes regardless. This preserves Gengar (our key win condition with Shadow Tag + Energy Ball for Rotom) while making progress on Metagross.
decisions.notebook: Bullet Punch (pri+1) from Metagross-Mega = guaranteed KO on Gengar-Mega at 37% (39.4-55.5%). Must always account for Bullet Punch priority when Gengar is low. Tyranitar Crunch at -1 Atk on Metagross = 26.7-43.9% (possible KO at 31%, not guaranteed). Incineroar Darkest Lariat = guaranteed KO on Gengar (96.4-140.1%). Fake Out should fail turn 5+ (Incineroar entered mid-turn 4). Houndoom Sucker Punch (pri+1, 161 Spe) can contest Metagross (130-162 Spe) in priority tier but Sucker Punch fails vs Protect. Next turn priorities: finish Metagross if it survives, then trap Rotom with Shadow Tag and KO with Energy Ball (may need Helping Hand for guaranteed KO at 82%). Save Houndoom for Serperior/Klefki matchups in games 2-3.

decisions.rationale: Fake Out (+3) flinches Tyranitar before it can Crunch Metagross. Bullet Punch (+1) hits Gengar before its Shadow Ball, with ~71.5% chance to KO from 37%. If Bullet Punch KOs, Metagross survives and we have 2v1 vs Tyranitar. If not, Gengar KOs Metagross but is then alone and weakened vs Incineroar + Rotom. No other line gives Metagross a chance to live through this turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Dragapult and Excadrill fainted. Opponent's last unrevealed is one of {Tauros-Aqua, Gholdengo, Houndoom}. Gengar-Mega has Shadow Tag — only pivot moves escape. Metagross holds our only Mega Stone; Mega Evolving grants Tough Claws. Incineroar carries Chople Berry and Intimidate, walls both Tyranitar and Gengar STABs. Sandstorm from Smooth Rock Tyranitar persists. Incineroar Fake Out used turn 5.

decisions.rationale: Gengar at 31% is guaranteed KO'd by Metagross Bullet Punch (priority +1) before it can act, and Protect's success rate is reduced after consecutive use. Switching Gengar to Houndoom is guaranteed safe: Houndoom walls both active foes (Bullet Punch 25-35.5%, Meteor Mash 55.9-78.9%, Darkest Lariat 30.3-44.7%, Flare Blitz immune via Flash Fire, Psychic Fangs immune via Dark typing). Tyranitar Crunch on Metagross (26.7-43.9% vs 31% HP) has a real chance to KO; even if it doesn't, Houndoom Flamethrower is a guaranteed KO on Metagross next turn (71.1-127.7%). If opponent Bullet Punches the Gengar slot (most likely since they know it's a KO), it hits Houndoom for negligible 0.5x damage. Worst case: opponent predicts switch and Meteor Mashes Tyranitar (64.7-92.8%), but Tyranitar survives at 96% HP.
decisions.notebook: Houndoom Flamethrower = guaranteed KO on Metagross-Mega at 31% (71.1-127.7%, 2x SE Fire vs Steel). Houndoom walls Metagross-Mega entirely: Bullet Punch 25-35.5%, Meteor Mash 55.9-78.9%, Psychic Fangs immune (Dark), and walls Incineroar: Darkest Lariat 30.3-44.7% (0.5x), Flare Blitz immune (Flash Fire). Tyranitar Crunch at -1 Atk on Metagross = 26.7-43.9% (possible KO at 31%, not guaranteed). Metagross Meteor Mash on Tyranitar = 64.7-92.8% (survives at 96% but drops to 3-31%). Houndoom Sucker Punch (pri+1, 161 Spe) contests Metagross (130-162 Spe) in priority tier but fails vs Protect. Save Houndoom for Serperior/Klefki matchups in games 2-3. Next turn priorities: finish Metagross with Houndoom Flamethrower (guaranteed KO), then trap Rotom with Shadow Tag (if Gengar still alive) or pressure with Houndoom/Tyranitar.

decisions.rationale: Metagross Protect blocks both Gengar Shadow Ball and Tyranitar Crunch, which would otherwise OHKO Metagross. Incineroar Darkest Lariat guarantees the KO on Gengar-Mega (73-142% into 31% HP), removing the faster Ghost-type threat. Gengar's Protect is only ~33% after two consecutive uses; even if it works, Metagross remains safe and we maintain board control. This preserves our Mega and eliminates their special attacker, leaving a 2v1 against Tyranitar and the unrevealed mon.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Dragapult and Excadrill fainted. Opponent's last unrevealed is one of {Tauros-Aqua, Gholdengo, Houndoom}. Gengar-Mega has Shadow Tag — only pivot moves escape. Metagross holds our only Mega Stone; Mega Evolving grants Tough Claws. Incineroar carries Chople Berry and Intimidate, walls both Tyranitar and Gengar STABs. Sandstorm from Smooth Rock Tyranitar persists. Incineroar Fake Out used turn 5. Metagross Protect used turn 4 (next use ~50%). Gengar Protect used turns 3 and 5 (next use ~33%).

decisions.rationale: Houndoom Flamethrower guarantees KO on Metagross-Mega at 31% (71.1-127.7%). Metagross just Protected last turn so consecutive Protect is unreliable — it will likely attack, and Meteor Mash on Tyranitar does 64.7-92.8% (drops to 3-31%). Tyranitar Protect blocks this, preserving HP for the Rotom-Wash endgame. Even if Metagross targets Houndoom with Bullet Punch instead (25-35.5%), Houndoom survives and still KOs Metagross. If Incineroar Parting Shots to Rotom, Tyranitar avoids the stat drop via Protect.
decisions.notebook: Houndoom Flamethrower = guaranteed KO on Metagross-Mega at 31% (71.1-127.7%). Metagross Meteor Mash on Tyranitar = 64.7-92.8% (survives at 96% but drops to 3-31%). Houndoom walls Metagross-Mega: Bullet Punch 25-35.5%, Meteor Mash 55.9-78.9%, Psychic Fangs immune. Houndoom walls Incineroar: Darkest Lariat 30.3-44.7% (0.5x), Flare Blitz immune (Flash Fire). Tyranitar Crunch at -1 Atk on Metagross = 26.7-43.9%. Save Houndoom for Serperior/Klefki matchups in games 2-3. Gengar-Mega at 31% with Shadow Tag for late-game trapping. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump is SE on both Tyranitar (2x Water vs Rock) and Houndoom (2x Water vs Fire) — preserve Tyranitar HP for endgame.

decisions.rationale: Metagross is guaranteed to be KO'd by Houndoom this turn (Flamethrower/Dark Pulse both OHKO from 31%). Bullet Punch (+1 priority) guarantees chip on Tyranitar (34.8-61.7%) before Metagross falls. Incineroar's Parting Shot onto Houndoom lowers its SpA/Atk by 1, neutering its threat to incoming Rotom-Wash, then pivots Incineroar out safely. Rotom enters against a debuffed Houndoom and damaged Tyranitar; Hydro Pump OHKOs Houndoom and Dark Pulse OHKOs the back Gengar-Mega from 31%. This preserves Incineroar as a late-game win condition while Rotom cleans up.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Dragapult and Excadrill fainted. Gengar-Mega has Shadow Tag. Metagross holds our only Mega Stone. Incineroar carries Chople Berry and Intimidate. Sandstorm from Smooth Rock Tyranitar. Incineroar Fake Out used turn 5. Metagross Protect used turns 4 and 6 (next use ~33%). Gengar Protect used turns 3 and 5 (next use ~33%). Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump OHKOs Houndoom; Dark Pulse OHKOs Gengar-Mega from range. Incineroar walls Tyranitar and Gengar STABs.

Helping Hand (priority +5) always resolves before Fake Out (priority +3), guaranteeing the boost even if Tyranitar is flinched. Houndoom (Speed 161) outspeeds Rotom-Wash (106-138), so boosted Dark Pulse (38.2-72%) lands before Rotom can Hydro Pump. Even if Houndoom falls to Hydro Pump, Rotom is left at 5-39% (+Sitrus = 30-64%), easily cleaned up by Gengar's Energy Ball (61-114%) or Tyranitar next turn. If opponent instead Fake Outs Houndoom, Houndoom survives at ~32% and Fake Out is consumed — next turn Houndoom attacks freely. Tyranitar at 96% is preserved for endgame in all scenarios. Switching to Gengar loses tempo (can't act on switch-in turn) and drops Houndoom's damage to 25.5-48% without Helping Hand.
decisions.notebook: Houndoom Flamethrower = guaranteed KO on Metagross-Mega at 31% (71.1-127.7%). Houndoom walls Metagross-Mega: Bullet Punch 25-35.5%, Meteor Mash 55.9-78.9%, Psychic Fangs immune. Houndoom walls Incineroar: Darkest Lariat 30.3-44.7% (0.5x), Flare Blitz immune (Flash Fire). Tyranitar Crunch at -1 Atk on Metagross = 26.7-43.9%. At -2 Atk: Crunch on Rotom-Wash = 15.3-27.2%, Rock Slide negligible. Gengar-Mega Energy Ball on Rotom-Wash = 61.1-113.6% (SE Grass vs Water). Helping Hand + Houndoom Dark Pulse on Rotom-Wash = 38.2-72%. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump: guaranteed KO on Houndoom (111.8-167.1%), 46.4-69.6% on Tyranitar (survives from 96%). Incineroar Flare Blitz on Tyranitar = 12.6-18.4% (NVE). Save Houndoom for Serperior/Klefki matchups in games 2-3. Gengar-Mega at 31% with Shadow Tag for late-game trapping. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump is SE on both Tyranitar (2x Water vs Rock) and Houndoom (2x Water vs Fire) — preserve Tyranitar HP for endgame. Switching Tyranitar out resets Intimidate stat drops.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Fake Out on Tyranitar prevents Rock Slide spread damage and Helping Hand. Hydro Pump on Houndoom guarantees a KO whether Houndoom stays (OHKO), Protects (wastes PP but Tyranitar flinched), or switches to Gengar-Mega (Hydro Pump also OHKOs Gengar-Mega). Houndoom moves before Rotom-Wash but its attacks are manageable (max ~38% Dark Pulse to Rotom). This line maximizes our advantage regardless of opponent's response.
decisions.notebook: Game 1: Dragapult and Metagross-Mega fainted. Incineroar and Rotom-Wash remain. Opponent has Tyranitar (95%, -2 Atk), Houndoom (33%, -2 Atk, -1 SpA), and Gengar-Mega (31%) in back. Gengar-Mega has Shadow Tag. Sandstorm ends after turn 8. Rotom-Wash Hydro Pump OHKOs both Houndoom and Gengar-Mega. Dark Pulse also OHKOs Gengar-Mega. Incineroar Fake Out re-enabled after Parting Shot switch.

decisions.rationale: Gengar at 31% is KO'd by any SE Dark move from either foe, so Protect is mandatory for survival. The opponent's most likely play is Rotom Protect + Incineroar Darkest Lariat on Gengar; if Gengar attacks instead, Energy Ball is wasted into Protect and Gengar dies for nothing. By Protecting, we waste both their turns while Tyranitar Rock Slide chips Incineroar (17.8-32.9% SE at -2 Atk) and Rotom (10.2-19.2%). Shadow Tag traps both foes, letting us repeat this pattern to grind down Incineroar.
